claim: Mutation settlement is not causally tied to the mutation: any SnapshotChanged clears every pending settle claim, and the 250 ms grace expiry releases a claim regardless, so await idle can return on stale daemon-derived state.

Teardown failures are collected after the scenario outcome is fixed: the failed journal entry and report are written from the pre-teardown outcome, home/ is deleted on the success branch, and only afterwards is the teardown problem turned into an error.

A directory run with an explicit --run-dir uses it as the suite root without creating or atomically claiming it (first child fails with NotFound, or a pre-created dir bypasses collision protection); the default suite root is created with the single-run layout, leaving stray home/, shots/, dumps/.

A shot whose app response succeeded but whose capture/baseline step later fails loses the app exchange from the journal: the later error propagates with ? and journal_outcome records only a runner error.

daemon restart: the adopted replacement is a shell gated on stdin when the PID seal is removed; Fleet (which auto-starts daemons) can win the race and acquire the singleton, so readiness succeeds against an unowned daemon and the adopted child exits.

The virtual lane pins output geometry through the Lua-only hyprctl eval hl.monitor(...) path before config-provider detection runs, so on a legacy/hyprlang-configured Hyprland the lane cannot pin geometry and falls back, contrary to the documented dual-provider support.

With --update-baselines every non-virtual lane skips capture entirely; in the attach lane (which has pixels) a shot succeeds and journals not-recorded against a PNG that was never written, so no screenshot artifact exists.

The Jobs log-follow loop keeps its reply receiver alive across the 250 ms TAIL_INTERVAL timer; because the bridge now holds the in-flight claim until the receiver closes, in_flight_requests never reaches zero while a log is followed and await idle times out.

lists.jobs is filtered by jobs_panel.filter but its filter field is always serialized as an empty string, so a scenario cannot observe the active filter and an empty filtered list is indistinguishable from an empty registry.
